learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the foundational rules formulated by management pioneers like Fayol and Taylor to run businesses scientifically and smoothly!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Principles are broad and general guidelines for decision-making. They are universally applicable, flexible, formed by practice and experimentation, and contingent on the situation.
Henri Fayol provided 14 principles like Division of Work (specialization), Unity of Command (one boss per employee), and Scalar Chain (formal line of authority).
F.W. Taylor believed there is 'one best way' to do a job. His principles include: Science not Rule of Thumb, Harmony not Discord, and Maximum Output.
Taylor introduced techniques like Functional Foremanship (8 specialists supervising), Time Study, Motion Study, and Differential Piece Wage System (paying efficient workers more).
Fayol's principles are applicable at the top level and focus on general administration. Taylor's focus is at the shop-floor (factory) level and emphasizes worker efficiency.

fun_activity.title: 🏭 The Paper Plane Assembly Line
fun_activity.instructions: Try making 10 paper planes all by yourself and time it. Then, gather 3 friends: one folds in half, one folds the wings, one throws. See how 'Division of Work' drastically speeds up production!

exam_tips: 📌 Do not confuse Unity of Command (one employee receives orders from ONLY ONE boss) with Unity of Direction (one unit, one plan).
📌 Remember the 'Gang Plank' concept in Scalar Chain—it allows direct communication between employees of the same level in an emergency.
📌 Case studies love to ask about 'Functional Foremanship'—remember it violates the principle of Unity of Command!
quick_recap: ⭐ Henri Fayol is known as the Father of General Management.
⭐ F.W. Taylor is known as the Father of Scientific Management.
⭐ Management principles are not rigid like scientific laws; they deal with human behavior and need flexibility.
